hpi: This case is a great illustration of the goal with a diagnosis of malrotation. Malrotation occurs as a result of an abnormality of the intestinal gut during embryogenesis. Volvulus occurs when the small bowel twists around itself, causing obstruction. This can lead to ischemia and obstruction. In this case, obstruction was seen by X-rays showing the intestinal loops, and potentially leading to dehydration and necrosis due to the vessels supplying blood to the bowel being cut off. The patient's slow rise in vital signs can lead to severe dehydration as potential hemorrhagic components. The important part of this case is to diagnose the problem quickly and ensure that the diagnosis is made, after which the patient should be stabilized with NG tube decompression and IV fluid resuscitation prior to surgery.
